threads.body: `streamClosed()` returns early when `!emitStableRpcSemconv()`, which means unknown/unregistered gRPC requests still won't produce a server span under the default configuration (old RPC semconv only). That seems to undermine the stated goal of capturing unknown service requests (issue #15690). Consider creating the fallback server span regardless of semconv stability, and populate whichever semconv flavor(s) are enabled (or at least emit the span + status) so the fix applies without requiring stable RPC semconv opt-in.

replies.body: This is intentional — the goal is to preserve the old behavior and only enable the new fallback span for unknown/unregistered services under the stable RPC semconv flag.

threads.body: `createServerInterceptor()` dereferences `serverInterceptorFactory` without checking for initialization, so callers will get a NullPointerException if `setServerInterceptorFactory()` hasn't run (e.g., if `Internal` is used without first loading `GrpcTelemetry`). Since this is a public method, please add a null check and fail fast with a clear IllegalStateException (and/or a safe default) to avoid an opaque NPE.

replies.body: Adopted the pattern used in #18291: marked the field `@Nullable`, switched to `requireNonNull(serverInterceptorFactory, "serverInterceptorFactory")`, and added a comment explaining why it's guaranteed non-null (registered in `GrpcTelemetry`'s static initializer, before any `GrpcTelemetry` instance can be passed here).

threads.body: The explanatory comment says unregistered services result in an HTTP-level response "rather than gRPC UNIMPLEMENTED", but the assertions below expect the client span to have `Status.Code.UNIMPLEMENTED`. Please reconcile this (e.g., clarify that Armeria returns HTTP 404 and the gRPC client maps that to UNIMPLEMENTED, and that there is no gRPC *server* span because the gRPC service layer isn't invoked).

replies.body: Reworded the comment to make this explicit (HTTP 404 mapped to UNIMPLEMENTED on the client, no gRPC server span because the gRPC service layer is never invoked). Pushed in 8846d666aa0.

threads.body: `GrpcRequest` is public and is exposed to user-provided `AttributesExtractor`s via `GrpcTelemetryBuilder`, but `getFullMethodName()` / `getOriginalFullMethodName()` are package-private while `getMethod()` is now nullable for the unknown-service fallback path. This leaves external extractors with no safe/public way to read the method name when `getMethod()` is null. Consider making these new getters public (and documenting when `getMethod()` may be null) so custom extractors can handle unregistered-method spans without NPEs or losing method information.

replies.body: Keeping public API minimal for now

threads.body: `streamClosed()` allocates a new `GrpcRequestGetter` for every unregistered request (`new GrpcRequestGetter()`). Since this code can run on every unknown-method call, consider reusing a static final getter instance (or otherwise avoiding per-request allocation) to reduce overhead on an already error-heavy path.

Disabling the thread-propagation debugger for *all* tests in this module can hide genuine context-leak regressions unrelated to the armeria HTTP+gRPC double-server-span scenario. If possible, scope this to only the affected test task(s) or test(s), or adjust instrumentation/test setup to avoid triggering the debugger while keeping it enabled for the rest of the suite.

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: The debugger setting is read when the test JVM starts, so JUnit cannot change it for one method. This module has one test class. Every test task runs grpcInstrumentation(), which triggers the Armeria HTTP and gRPC double-server-span case. The current setting is therefore already scoped to all affected test tasks. Splitting each semantic-convention suite into extra JVMs would add several test tasks only to run unknownService() with the debugger enabled.

Upsides: Keeping the setting on the existing test tasks avoids duplicate test suites and keeps all semantic-convention modes covered. The scope does not affect another test class.

Downsides: unknownService() also runs without the debugger. A future unrelated test in this module would need a separate task or a different test setup if it must run with the debugger enabled.

Upsides: The declaration now matches the repository rule and the sibling ArmeriaSingletons holder.

Downsides: No material downside identified.
